summary: 100-foot steel tower announced for Newport on the St. Marks River in 1937 by Florida forest officials, built by CCC enrollees; no source on its status today.

events.note: Tallahassee Democrat item dated January 17, 1937 says the construction work had been done and the tower would be raised 'some time Monday'. The item gives no finish date.

evidence.supports: Announced tower: 100-foot steel lookout tower at Newport, Wakulla county
evidence.quote: A 100-foot steel lookout tower will be raised some time Monday at Newport in Wakulla county

evidence.supports: Site on the east bank of the St. Marks River, opposite the town of Newport
evidence.quote: The tower is located on the east bank of the St Marks river just opposite the town of Newport

evidence.supports: 28-acre site given to the state by V.G. Phillips of Tallahassee
evidence.quote: in a 28-acre site which was donated to the state by V.G. Phillips, of Tallahassee

evidence.supports: Announcement by District Forest William F. Jacobs of the Florida forest service
evidence.quote: according to the announcement of District Forest William F. Jacobs, of the Florida forest service

evidence.supports: Construction done by CCC enrollees from side camp P-68A under Project Superintendent T.R. Demery
evidence.quote: The construction work has been done by CCC enrollees from ECW side camp P-68A under the supervision of Project Superintendent T.R. Demery

evidence.supports: The item is a Tallahassee Democrat report reproduced by Eastern US Lookouts

sources.title: Newport - FOREST LOOKOUTS (quoting a Tallahassee Democrat item of January 17, 1937)

notes_for_editor: One source only: a 1937 newspaper advance notice quoted on the Eastern US Lookouts page. Built year 1937 is the notice date: the item says construction was done by then but gives no finish date and no raising date. Height 30.5 m in the brief's record matches the announced 100 ft, but no source confirms the built height. No source found on status, access or fate today; status left as unknown. Searches turned up a CCC history of the St. Marks refuge and a 2015 Florida lookout report, but neither names this tower (the 2015 PDF has no Newport match). A search summary mentioned a Magnolia tower near Newport; that is a different tower and is not used. The FFS agency fact rests on the notice's 'Florida forest service' wording.
